title: Legaltech Hub: global legal technology and AI vendor directory
answer: Legaltech Hub is a global directory of legal technology solutions, tools and services, aimed at buyers, vendors and investors. Its most useful contribution is as a map of the market: it catalogues vendors and solutions, and its landing page also surfaces recent developments such as NetDocuments' Legal Context Graph, OpenAI's Astra for Law, Steno's Transcript Genius, MiAI Law and a piece on GenAI eroding junior lawyer training. For AI in Legal, it helps identify what exists before evaluating what works.

sections.body: Legaltech Hub publishes this page as the global directory of legal technology solutions, tools and services. It says buyers can research legal tech for a 21st century law firm or in-house department, vendors can showcase solutions, and investors can understand the marketplace. The page also carries short summaries of recent articles and interviews. No publication date is stated in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page describes Legaltech Hub as a global directory where buyers research legal technology, vendors showcase solutions, and investors understand the marketplace. Beyond that description, the supplied text presents several recent items. NetDocuments is building its AI strategy around a Legal Context Graph launched in May, with a new benchmark and two AI features, arguing that as models and legal tools become more interchangeable, advantage shifts to firms that connect AI to their own documents, knowledge and legal authorities. OpenAI has released Astra for Law, built initially for Am Law 200 firms, described not as a new model but a model configuration pairing its most recent GPT-6 Astra model with specific knowledge, tools and ecosystem plugins tailored for legal. Transcript Genius is a Steno deposition transcript analysis tool using AI to mine deposition and trial transcripts for summaries, data points and strategic insights. MiAI Law is an Australian legal AI platform combining case law research, legislative research, case summarization, contract review, and document and pleading verification, built for Australian legal practice. The page also notes a piece on GenAI taking over document review, first drafts and due diligence, and the concern that some automated work was how junior lawyers learned judgment through repetition, supervision and real matters, with firms experimenting with simulations and redesigned workflows.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Legaltech Hub defines itself as the global directory of legal technology solutions, tools and services. The text says NetDocuments launched its Legal Context Graph in May and added a new benchmark and two AI features. It says OpenAI's Astra for Law was built initially for Am Law 200 firms and pairs the GPT-6 Astra model with legal-specific knowledge, tools and ecosystem plugins. It describes Transcript Genius as a Steno tool for deposition transcript analysis. It describes MiAI Law as an Australian legal AI platform covering case law research, legislative research, case summarization, contract review, and document and pleading verification. The text gives no market size, adoption rate or performance figures.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Legal can use this source as a starting map of vendors and tools, because it catalogues global legal technology and AI offerings and points to recent examples such as NetDocuments, OpenAI, Steno and MiAI Law. It is useful before evaluating what works, as the industry page says, because it shows what exists and how vendors position AI for legal work. It also flags a workforce concern around GenAI and junior lawyer training, which is relevant to how firms adopt AI beyond efficiency.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: The supplied text is mostly a directory landing page with short article summaries, not a detailed report or independent evaluation. It does not provide methodology, pricing, rankings, performance data or dates for most items. It is commercial in the sense that vendors can showcase solutions, so descriptions may reflect vendor positioning. Coverage is partial and global in name, but the examples shown are limited to a few companies and one Australian platform. No publication date is stated.
